title: Data fiduciary obligations - a checklist every business needs
p1:
Your business may not sell customer data and still be responsible for protecting it.

Many companies assume privacy obligations only apply to big tech firms. The reality is different: any organisation collecting personal data can become responsible for how that information is handled.
p2:
A surprising fact: a data breach is not the only problem. Poor consent practices, excessive data collection, weak security measures, and unclear retention policies can also create serious compliance risks.

A data fiduciary is simply a business that decides why and how personal data is processed. That role comes with a duty of care toward the people whose data it uses.
p3:
A practical checklist starts with five questions: Do we collect only the data we need? Do people know how their data is used? Are security controls strong enough? Do we delete data when it is no longer needed? Can we respond quickly to privacy requests?

Privacy is no longer just a legal requirement; it is a trust factor that can influence customer decisions and business reputation.
conclusion: What is the biggest privacy challenge your organisation faces today: collecting data responsibly, securing it, or managing customer consent?
